title: Zaldy Co's 3 co-accused tagged as fugitives by Sandiganbayan
summary: The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division declared three co-accused of former lawmaker Zaldy Co as "fugitives" from justice in connection to graft charges.

blocks.text: The Sandiganbayan Fifth Division declared three co-accused of former lawmaker Zaldy Co as "fugitives" from justice in connection to graft charges.
In a six-page resolution promulgated on November 10, the anti-graft court also ordered the cancellation of passports of Timojen Sacar, Anthony Ngo, and Consuelo Aldon.
The ruling noted that the three individuals remained at large amid the arrest warrants and hold departure order issued against them on November 21, 2025.

"Given the high-profile nature of the case, it is reasonable to conclude that the accused are aware of the criminal proceedings and the outstanding warrants issued against them," the ruling penned by Associate Justice Zaldy Trespeses read.

"Thus, by stating beyond the reach of law enforcement while fully aware of pending warrants of arrest confirms accused's deliberate intent to evade judicial process. By choosing to remain at large for nearly a year, accused Sacar, Ngo, and Aldon have rendered themselves fugitives from justice," it added.
The anti-graft court also said that the cancellation of their passports "hinders attempts to evade judicial processes."

"The cancellation of fugitive's passport is an essential remedy to address the flight risk posed by individuals facing criminal charges, thereby safeguarding the administration of criminal justice," it ruled.
Co and the three fugitives are facing graft charges linked to alleged anomalies in flood-control and infrastructure projects.
The former Ako Bicol partylist representative also remains at large, though it was previously reported that he could be in Europe.
